title: Reading user input and validating conversion results
learningObjectives: Explain the language rule and its constraints.
Trace the example and predict its behaviour.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: Formatted input functions return the number of successful assignments. A program must check that count before using the destination objects. For robust line-oriented parsing, read a line and convert it with functions such as strtol while checking the end pointer and range.
understand.whyItMatters: This knowledge helps reason about C data representation, object bounds and valid memory access.
understand.analogy: Think of memory objects as labelled storage and pointers as typed references to that storage.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal pointer, lifetime and object-access rules.

explain.narrative:
Formatted input functions return the number of successful assignments. A program must check that count before using the destination objects. For robust line-oriented parsing, read a line and convert it with functions such as strtol while checking the end pointer and range.

Check the declared types, object lifetime, valid bounds and function preconditions before using the construct. Enable compiler warnings and test edge cases.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.code: Input is untrusted data. A failed conversion, trailing characters or a value outside the destination type's range must not be treated as a valid number.

practise.guidedTask: scanf needs the address of age because it writes the converted value there. The return value is checked before age is read. This simple example detects failed integer conversion; production input should also define how trailing input is handled.
practise.independentTask: What happens if the user enters letters instead of an integer?
hints: Write an input routine that rejects invalid input and explains how it handles trailing characters and out-of-range values.
The conversion count is not the same as the number of characters consumed.
Use strtol for more controlled integer parsing and inspect errno, endptr and range before narrowing.
